cascade_lake_8280.protocol: n=8 interleaved, single-threaded, all binaries validate 78498

assembly_findings.sparse_loop: koru __mm_sp_*: 8x orb + 2 adds + cmp = 12 instr/iter. rust reset_sparse: 8x orb + 8 ptr-adds + cmp = 21 instr/iter. Koru's is TIGHTER.
assembly_findings.dense_loop: instruction-identical SSE vectorized RMW (movups/orps/movups pairs + scalar or) both sides
assembly_findings.structure: same algorithm: dense unrolled word-mask sweep for strides <~129, 8-way byte-scatter for larger, both start marking at p^2
assembly_findings.perf_profile_clx: koru 63% of cycles in 4 sparse fns; IPC 1.05 vs rust 1.58; L1-misses 129k/pass vs 98k; instructions/pass 533k vs ~675k
assembly_findings.conclusion: no codegen deficit found — koru emits fewer, tighter instructions for identical work

rejected_levers: DENSE_LIMIT 128->512: -19% SKL, -34% ARM. Full-field sweeps cost more than strided marks save on every silicon tried.
prefetch 2-groups-ahead in sparse loop: -14% SKL, -10% ARM. 8 extra instrs/iter outweigh latency cover.

final_verdict.koru_vs_koru: PARITY — era vs head within ~1% on all three machines. The July->Oct perf work neither helped nor hurt this workload.
final_verdict.koru_vs_rust: SUPERSEDED by resolution: the x86 gap was compiler_rt memset; after the fix, parity on 8168/8280; ARM koru +11%
final_verdict.koru_variance: koru per-pass cost spans 33.6k-86k across machines; rust spans 39.4k-77.6k. Koru's strided-marker profile is more microarch-sensitive.
final_verdict.claim_status: the blog claim is hardware-dated — true on the measured CPU generation, not reproducible as a general statement

resolution.root_cause: std/field:new-heap zeroed via @memset, which links Zig compiler_rt's local memset (nm: 't memset') instead of glibc's; rust imports memset@GLIBC
resolution.fix: koru 78ef909c2 — zero through libc bzero when link_libc
resolution.fix_vs_rust: parity within 0.1-1%; koru won 3/18 interleaved rounds — not a win
resolution.isolation: calloc ~= bzero ~= rust; malloc-once + compiler_rt memset ~= before; field alignment offsets 0..2048 flat
corrections: cascade_lake_8280 27% gap came from a single droplet; two fresh 8280s gave 6.5% before the fix
MLP/fill-buffer hypothesis false: L1 misses, fb_full, and sparse cycles are equal per pass
earlier L1-miss 129k vs 98k compared rust's 10s perf window to koru's 5s
still_unmeasured: mechanism by which compiler_rt memset slows the subsequent dense sweeps

resolution_2_direction_alternation.root_cause: all ~170 marker sweeps per pass ran forward over a 62.5KB field; on 32KB L1D each sweep evicted the field before the next reuse — every line of every sweep came from L2
resolution_2_direction_alternation.fix: koru 2700a4366 — std/field markers take a direction; Field flips direction per mark when field bytes > runtime-queried L1D (sysconf glibc / sysctl Darwin; off when unknown); libc zeroing also for clear/on-stack
resolution_2_direction_alternation.arm_local: 85.9-86.8k — unchanged; 64KB L1D fits the field so alternation stays off; descending sweeps would cost 6-9% there
still_unmeasured: Ice Lake 8358 — no c-2 draw landed it
why descending sweeps cost 6-9% on ARM even when inactive codepath
resolution_2_direction_alternation.portability_caveat: alternating direction is ~20 lines; Rust could adopt it — the durable lead is that the fix lives in the stdlib transform, not in application code
